questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere I hadn't been before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took some time making sense of all of it, but generally it was pretty easy, and both KU and my host university were really helpful in giving out the information I needed beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lots of email correspondence with my host university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used AirBnB and can really recommend that, since Concordia University doesn't offer many student housing possibilities for exchange students (from what I could see).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will most likely need to pay for an Opus Card (which is for public transportation) and they cost around 1200 DKK for four months of unlimited travel with a student discount included.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Concordia doesn't really help much with finding student accommodation, but luckily there were a lot of options available in Montreal.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seems a bit confusing at first, but people are really fast and helpful at responding to emails asking questions, so I figured it out quickly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a student user account, add which courses you want to attend, get them approved, and then you're good to go. It's really easy and just a few clicks around on their website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email, call, student center, etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the International Students Office whenever you are confused about anything. They are super kind and helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Soooo many interesting courses!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Less readings than at KU, but the readings are generally more varied and interesting, in my opinion.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Concordia is a lot more international and progressive than UCPH. Though you should be aware that most students in Canada start university at around 18 years old, so people are generally quite young in the classes. I was definitely one of the oldest and I'm only 22.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Marketing and Sociology courses focusing on racial relations and culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything on Sociology

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Thermal underwear, cause Canada is cold. I was NOT ready for -20 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dairy products are pretty expensive but restaurants are generally cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many fun and cool clubs at Concordia!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many different clubs, club events, social events, etc. Literally something happening every single week, it's amazing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the clubs! And if you're an ethnic minority, join one of the minority student unions. I had a lot of fun in the Black Student Union.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can definitely recommend going to Toronto for a few days if you ever have the opportunity. Don't go in the CN tower though. It's super expensive and not worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be yourself and be open

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is much more diversity in Montreal (and Canada in general) than in Denmark and people seem more culturally openminded. I really appreciated that, especially as a POC.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be prepared for really cold winters
2) Join as many clubs as possible (you don't have to go to all of their events, but if you join them, at least you'll know whenever something fun is happening)
3) Be prepared to study with people who are a lot younger than you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made and all of the new perspectives I gained from the courses I took.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: One of my teachers had a teaching style that relied very heavily on physical class attendance and note-sharing among students which can be annoying if you prefer doing most of the studying at home by yourself, but the courses are usually only one class per week, so although it was irritating, it was manageable.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Remember to have fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
